description: Base Renovate preset for Polarion repositories maintained by the SBB Polarion Team

packageRules.description: Automerge non-major updates (minor, patch, pin, digest)
Major updates require manual review (potential breaking changes)
Internal SBB packages and container images - skip the minimum-release-age stability wait (automerge per the rules above: minor/patch auto, major manual)

Docker and GitHub Actions tags frequently lack a release timestamp, so under the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required they get stuck as 'pending' status checks and never create branches/PRs. Treat them as stable without a timestamp so they flow through the automerge rules above; timestamped datasources (e.g. pypi, npm) keep the strict minimumReleaseAge wait
Automerge GitHub Actions updates including major versions - group into one branch/PR
Automerge pre-commit updates including major versions - group into one branch/PR
Skip pinning for org-internal reusable workflows (tracked on @main intentionally)

vitest-browser-react must move in the same branch as the vitest monorepo. It declares a peer dependency on an exact vitest major, so a vitest major update that leaves it behind makes the tree unresolvable: npm refuses the peer set, Renovate cannot regenerate the lock file, and the pull request lands with the manifest bumped and package-lock.json untouched, which fails every `npm ci`. The vitest 4 to 5 update did exactly that across this estate. Renovate's own monorepo grouping cannot cover the package, because it is published outside vitest-dev/vitest.

Type every dependency update `fix`. This overrides :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers, reached through config:best-practices > config:recommended, which types only runtime dependencies `fix` (Maven compile/provided/runtime/system/import/parent, pep621 and poetry project dependencies, npm dependencies) and everything else `chore` - so test-scoped Maven deps, dev dependency groups and npm devDependencies read `chore` while the identical library read `fix` elsewhere. A single type makes the dependency history uniform across every ecosystem in this estate. This MUST be a packageRule and not a top-level semanticCommitType: the upstream `chore` assignments are themselves packageRules, and a packageRule always beats top-level config. Note this rule cannot reach an update with no package name - PackageNameMatcher returns false on a falsy packageName before the `*` short-circuit - so lockFileMaintenance is untouched by it and needs no carve-out. The carve-outs below must stay AFTER this rule, because packageRules are applied in array order and the last match wins.

Workflow action updates stay `chore` against the rule above - they change build infrastructure, never anything the product ships, so they must not read as a fix to a consumer scanning the history or a generated changelog.
Pre-commit hook updates stay `chore` for the same reason as the workflow actions: the hooks are commit-gate tooling and are not part of any build output.

Same for a lock-file-only update of a dependency whose declared range already allowed the new version - the manifest is untouched. This restores the one lockfile carve-out :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers actually has - its rules are `*` to chore, four matchDepTypes rules to fix, and this one. There is no lockFileMaintenance rule upstream and none is needed here either, because that update carries no package name and the `*` rule above cannot reach it.
